title: The Beauty Queen Of Leenane - review
transcript: hello and welcome to one minute theater reviews i'm paul seven lewis this is the minerva theater at chichester and i'm here to review the beauty queen of lenon we've come to know martin mcdonough very well over the last 25 years uh revivals of his plays the crippler finnish man with daniel radcliffe and the lieutenant of inish moore with uh aidan turner were west end triumphs that have really cemented his playwriting reputation but they've been other hits like hangmen and a very very very dark matter and then there is films in bruges and three billboards outside ebbing missouri and others i guess you either love him i hate him but personally i love him for his unpredictable storytelling his humorous dialogue and sudden violent shocks and it's all here in his first play the beauty queen of lennan revived here in a co-production by chester chichester festival theatre and the lyric hammersmith the play centers on the relationship between seventy-year-old mag played by ingrid craigie and her 40-year-old daughter and carer maureen played by all of its gerald the pair of them isolated in a run-down irish village back in the 1990s they only have each other and this dependencies led to a toxic indeed abusive relationship in which each torments the other in small sometimes significant ways mag empties her chamber pot into the kitchen sink each morning to the annoyance of her daughter maureen only buys biscuits that she knows her mother dislikes it reminded me of the co-dependent parent-child relationship that formed the heart of stepton's son if you remember that tv sitcom max schemes to undermine maureen in order to keep her at home destroying important notes and letters the mentally unstable daughter having apparently sacrificed her life to perform her filial duty crosses from care to cruelty the relationship is dark sinister even but the interplay between them is also very amusing both actors convince in the ease of their conversation which sounds like they've been having the same exchanges for the last 20 years much like in a beckett or pinter play i particularly enjoyed the the animation and look of secret triumph that ingrid craigie gave as mag when she had secret knowledge about the truth of a situation and mischievously led on maureen in her lie about it and all of its journal was tremendous whenever she tried to lord it over her mother stepping out with hips swaying the co-dependency is threatened when pato appears on the scene although a local he's also an outsider having emigrated to london and england is always seen as a lion influence in this play the place that has destroyed ireland and continues to ruin this village it's a relationship perhaps not dissimilar to that of magmori anyway this outsider forms a liaison with maureen whom he calls his beauty queen and threatens to take her away to the promised land of america but not if mag has anything to do with it a violent and unhappy end seems inevitable and adam best is very moving as pato a sad lonely man isolated by his irish village origins in the prejudiced and dangerous world of english building sites at the beginning of act two he writes a letter to maureen about his life and dreams that is truly heartbreaking the fourth member of the cast is kwaku fortune who convincingly portrays pato's brother ray his main role is that of a miserable messenger but in his short scenes he convincingly portrays the dead end nature of life in linan which for him lies mainly in an obsession with australian soaps and a surly attitude the set by good teeth theater was dingy in a way that you could almost smell the urine and the rainy black and white backbone back wall projection was appropriately bleak strangely for a venue as intimate as the minerva the set was spread out with mag's armchair and a stove on one side and maureen's chair and kitchen area on the other which suggested a boxing ring in which each protagonist had their corner at the sound by an o'clock that accompanied the scenes was equally come to the scene breaks was equally desolate martin mcdonough certainly has a way with words and if the beauty queen of lennan isn't as laugh out loud funny nor as original in its subject matter as his later work it is still absorbing and rachel oren's production does it proud i give the beauty queen of linan three stars i hope you've enjoyed this review or at least found it interesting and if you did and you want to be the first to know about my future reviews please subscribe to this channel by clicking on the button below and if you want to read my reviews go to my website one minute theater reviews theaterreviews.co.uk thank you for watching
